Build and query models

Source: R/models.R
z3_model_set.Rd

z3_model(ctx) creates an empty model. z3_model_set() assigns a value to a constant; z3_model_set_function() defines a function by a table of entries and a default value. z3_model_set_default() replaces the default (else) value of a function the model already interprets and keeps its entries; it works on models returned by solvers too. The default value of a function may use z3_bound_var() i for argument i + 1. A hand-made model can be used with z3_eval() to evaluate expressions under chosen values.

Usage

z3_model_set(model, constant, value)

z3_model_set_function(model, f, entries = list(), otherwise)

z3_model_set_default(model, f, otherwise)

z3_model_has(model, x)

z3_model_universes(model)

z3_as_array_function(x)

Arguments

model

A z3_model.

constant

A constant (z3_expr).

value

A value of the constant's sort.

f

A z3_function or z3_func_decl.

entries

A list of entries, each list(args = list(...), value = v).

otherwise

The value for all other arguments.

x

A constant, function, or (for z3_as_array_function()) an array value.

Value

z3_model_set(), z3_model_set_function() and z3_model_set_default() return model invisibly; the others return the requested information.

Details

z3_model_has() tests whether a model interprets a constant or function. z3_model_universes() returns, for each uninterpreted sort of the model, the finite list of values the model uses for it. z3_as_array_function() returns the function behind an array value of the form (_ as-array f), or NULL.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
f <- z3_function(ctx, "f", z3_int_sort(ctx), z3_int_sort(ctx))
m <- z3_model(ctx)
z3_model_set(m, x, 5)
z3_model_set_function(m, f, list(list(args = list(5), value = 50)), 0)
z3_eval(m, f(x) + f(1))
#> <z3_expr Int> 50
z3_model_set_default(m, f, z3_bound_var(ctx, 0, z3_int_sort(ctx)) * 2)
z3_eval(m, f(x) + f(1))
#> <z3_expr Int> 52
